_doc: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every container that touches the GPU.
Consumers (all derive from this file — do not hardcode container names):
services/router/app/config.py        -> VLLM_MODELS / GPU_SERVICES
services/router/app/core/router_engine.py -> exclusivity switching
services/router/app/api/routes/gpu.py     -> /gpu whitelist + modes
services/webapp/main.py              -> /gpu panel, /logs, queue page
scripts/service.sh                   -> compose --profile flags (via jq)
To add a GPU container: add an entry here, AND add the matching service to
docker-compose.yml. Compose cannot read this file (profiles must be literal
in the YAML), so that one definition stays duplicated — nothing else does.
Field reference:
container       Docker container_name, must match docker-compose.yml exactly.
compose_service Service key in docker-compose.yml (differs from the registry
id for vLLM: id 'qwen-32b' -> service 'vllm-qwen').
display_name    Human label shown in the WebUI.
type            'vllm'    = an OpenAI-compatible LLM server (has base_url,
model_path, aliases; Router routes chat to it).
'service' = anything else with a GPU reservation.
profile         Compose profile that gates it, or null to start with a plain
`docker compose up -d`. Non-null means the container is NOT
auto-started: compose only creates it, and the Router owns
start/stop. This is what keeps two GPU hogs off one card —
the profile is not a lock, it just keeps compose from
starting something the Router is supposed to schedule.
exclusive       true  = needs the whole card; starting it stops every other
exclusive entry (24 GB RTX 3090, no MIG).
false = small enough to coexist (e.g. Whisper at ~4 GB).
startup_sec     Rough cold-start estimate, used for WebUI progress hints.
